lessons.title: Getting the horse and the clippers ready
lessons.html:
Why we clip

Some horses grow a thick winter coat. When they work hard, they sweat and stay wet for a long time. This can make them cold and sick. Clipping removes some of the hair so the horse dries quickly. A clipped horse needs a rug at night and in cold weather.

Prepare the horse

  1. Choose a dry, well-lit place with a non-slip floor and no water near the cables.
  2. Tie the horse with a quick-release knot, or ask a helper to hold it.
  3. Groom the horse well. The coat must be clean and dry. Dirt and sweat blunt the blades and pull the hair.
  4. Check the coat for cuts, lumps or ticks. Do not clip over a wound.
  5. Mark the lines of the clip with chalk if needed.
  6. If the horse has never been clipped, let it hear and feel the clippers first, slowly, on the shoulder.

Prepare the clippers

Always read the manufacturer's instructions for your clippers.

  • Check the cable and plug. Never use clippers with a damaged cable. Use an earth leakage plug where possible.
  • Check that the blades are sharp and clean, and fitted the right way.
  • Set the blade tension as the manufacturer says. Too tight makes the blades hot; too loose pulls the hair.
  • Oil the blades with clipper oil before you start.
  • Test the clippers away from the horse.

Your own safety

  • Wear closed shoes and tie back long hair. No loose clothes.
  • Keep the cable away from the horse's feet.
  • Stand to the side of the horse, never directly behind it.

lessons.title: Clipping technique and care of the clippers
lessons.html:
Types of clip

ClipWhat is removedFor which horse
Bib clipFront of neck and chestLight work
Trace clipUnderside of neck, belly and upper legsMedium work
Blanket clipNeck and sides; a blanket shape is left on the backMedium to hard work
Hunter clipAll the coat except legs and saddle patchHard work
Full clipAll the coatVery hard work, show horses

How to clip

  1. Start on the shoulder, where most horses accept it.
  2. Clip against the direction of the hair, with long, even strokes.
  3. Keep the blades flat on the skin. Do not dig in the points.
  4. Stretch loose skin, for example behind the elbow, with your free hand.
  5. Feel the blades often. If they get hot, stop, let them cool, brush off hair and oil again.
  6. Do sensitive areas like the head, belly and between the legs last, with a helper holding the horse.
  7. Make both sides match.
  8. Brush off loose hair and put on a rug.

Never

  • Never clip a wet horse.
  • Never clip inside the ears; it protects them from insects.
  • Never pull the clippers by the cable.

Care of the clippers after use

  • Unplug first.
  • Remove the blades and brush out all hair.
  • Clean the blades with blade wash, dry them, and oil them.
  • Clean the air filter as the manual says.
  • Coil the cable loosely and store the clippers in their box in a dry place.
  • Send blunt blades for sharpening.

Key points

  • Only clip a clean, dry horse.
  • Check the cable and blades before use; never use a damaged cable.
  • Clip against the hair with flat, even strokes.
  • Stop when blades get hot; cool and oil them.
  • Clean, oil and store clippers after use; rug the clipped horse.
